vignette: Kai had always taken pride in his work as a chef, whipping up traditional Samoan dishes with ease and flair. But that was before the night he was raped by a coworker after a late-night shift at the restaurant. Kai's memories of that evening were fragmented and disordered - he could recall the feeling of being pinned down, the sound of his attacker's laughter, but the events leading up to and following the assault were hazy. As time passed, Kai found himself pushing away any attempts to fully recall the details of that night. He'd start to think about it, only to quickly shut down the memory before it could fully surface. It was as if his mind was trying to protect him from something, but this avoidance came at a cost. Kai began to feel like he was no longer capable of doing the things that defined him - cooking with passion and creativity. He'd catch himself standing in front of the stove, staring blankly at a pot of boiling water, unsure of how to proceed. Kai's feelings of contamination were palpable. He'd scrub his hands raw after every meal prep, unable to shake the feeling that he was somehow dirty or tainted. This sense of dirtiness extended beyond his physical body - he felt like the trauma had seeped into every aspect of his life, destroying everything he held dear. As a result, Kai began to withdraw from his friends and family. He stopped attending traditional Samoan ceremonies, where food played a central role in celebrations. He couldn't bear the thought of being around others, fearing that they'd somehow sense his contamination. His relationships suffered, including his relationship with his ex-wife, who eventually left him due to his increasing isolation. At work, Kai's avoidance behaviors started to take a toll on his performance. He'd shy away from certain ingredients or cooking techniques that reminded him of the assault. His boss began to notice the decline in quality and creativity of Kai's dishes, and the restaurant's owner started to wonder if it was time to let him go. Despite his best efforts to keep the memories at bay, they continued to seep into his daily life. A certain smell - the scent of coconut oil - would transport him back to that terrible night. The sound of laughter from the kitchen staff would make him feel like he was reliving the trauma all over again. It wasn't until Kai received a court summons to testify against his attacker that he realized he needed help. The thought of facing his rapist in court, of having to relive those memories in front of strangers, sent him into a panic. What frightened him most was the fear of losing control, of breaking down in public. Kai finally sought out therapy, hoping to find a way to reclaim his life and his sense of self. As he sat in the therapist's office, he couldn't help but wonder - would he ever be able to cook with passion again? Would he ever feel clean? Or was his life forever destroyed by the trauma?
